name: Hepher
overview: Hepher was a male member of the tribe of Manasseh, identified uniquely as the son of Gilead. He is noted in Scripture as the progenitor of the Hepherites, a clan within Manasseh. This designation situates Hepher within the genealogical records of Israel, emphasizing his role in the tribal lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Hepher is a proper name that possibly means 'help.' There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries a meaning that may reflect a characteristic or hoped-for attribute.
familyAndRelationships: Hepher is explicitly recorded as the son of Gilead. Additionally, it is inferred that Zelophehad was his father, linking Hepher to a notable family line within Manasseh. Beyond these relationships, Scripture does not provide further familial details.
scriptureSignificance: Hepher's significance lies in his role as the ancestor of the Hepherites, a distinct clan within the tribe of Manasseh. His lineage contributes to the detailed genealogical records essential for understanding Israel's tribal divisions and inheritance. This highlights God's providential preservation of His people through careful record-keeping of family lines.
